The coconut based cleansers used in it gently clean the hair making it suitable for daily use. 200 ml of Moms and Company's Natural [00:03:20] Protein Shampoo will cost you rupees 429. This shampoo is really worth the price. Finally, ranked at number one is Rustic Arts Biodegradable Aloe Shampoo. Handmade with goodness of coconut, bermuda grass and wheat protein. This [00:03:36] shampoo is thick in consistency and promises to leave your hair shiny and strengthened. This shampoo is not only free from harsh chemicals but also is budget friendly. 200 ml of rustic cards aloe shampoo will cost you just rupees [00:03:51] 290. Moreover, the shampoo is suitable for all hair types. So, because it is easily affordable and free from toxins, it tops my list. Although all these five shampoos mentioned are toxin-free, safe and highly recommended. Moreover, you [00:04:07] can be proud of the fact that all these five shampoos that we have discussed are made by Indian brands. The links to all these shampoos are in the description box. segments.text: [00:00:03] Which shampoo do you use? Dove, Pantene, L'Oreal, or Sunsilk? Have you ever read the ingredient list of your shampoo? If you haven't, then let me tell you this. It's scary. There are many toxic chemicals in shampoos which are linked to hair fall, irritation, illness, and even cancer. And if you are unknowingly [00:00:20] using a shampoo which is toxic, it is doing more harm to your hair than good. Using such shampoo will gradually weaken your hair and you may face issues like dandruff, hair fall, and even diseases. It is very important to use a shampoo which is gentle on the hair and the [00:00:36] underlying skin. So, which shampoo is the best? Let us find out. Hello friends, welcome to FitTuber. For this video, I bought almost 20 shampoos. Some from the supermarket while others [00:00:52] online. I thoroughly examined each and every ingredient on all these shampoos and was quite disappointed. You too will be shocked to know that the most popular shampoos which are used by the majority of Indians have the maximum number of toxic chemicals in them. And when I say [00:01:09] toxic, I mean they are really damaging. These ingredients include detergents, petroleum products, insecticides, pesticides, and what not. One more thing which I noticed during the intensive research of this video was that the ingredients in the different varieties [00:01:26] of the same brand were almost the same. I have divided all these 20 shampoos into four categories on the basis of number of harmful chemicals in them. So, let us see in which category do all these shampoos fall in. Category number one include shampoos like Garnier, [00:01:42] Tresemme, Head & Shoulders, L'Oreal, Pantene Pro-V, Dove, Clinic Plus, Sunsilk, All Clear, which have more than 10 toxic chemicals in them. These, in my opinion, are the worst of the kind. It [00:01:58] is so disappointing to know that the shampoo brands which we have been trusting since childhood are the main villains. Not only these, but the so-called herbal shampoo by Himalaya also falls in this category. Other herbal shampoos like Dabur Vatika and [00:02:13] Nile Naturals are no different. Even the not so popular herbal shampoos like Kesh King, Meera and Karthika are no good. We all know that beer is good for washing hair. However, this made from real beer shampoo by Park Avenue is truly [00:02:28] disappointing. All these shampoos have everything which is harmful for your hair, including strong fragrances and artificial colors. Coming to category number two, which includes shampoos like Johnson's Baby and Wow's Apple Cider Vinegar Shampoo. These are a little [00:02:45] better than the category number one, but are still far from the best. If we compare these two shampoos with each other, Wow is better as it is free from sulfates. Overall, they have around six to seven toxic chemicals including artificial fragrances and colors. In [00:03:01] category number three falls shampoos like Ayush, Biotique and Patanjali. These are the shampoos which are trying to fool their customers using oversmart marketing tactics. All these shampoos mention only 10% of the ingredients on the bottle. I don't understand if your [00:03:17] shampoo is made from 100% botanical extracts, then why do you have to hide 90% of its ingredients? And what is the reason that the 90% of the ingredients of your shampoo fall in the soap base to which the customer has no access? If [00:03:33] only 10% of the ingredients in your shampoo are from natural herbs, it doesn't make that shampoo an Ayurvedic medicine, does it? At least the shampoos in category number one are frank about their ingredients. Such malpractices doesn't make these shampoos trustworthy. [00:03:49] Ayush shampoo, although has mentioned three preservatives used in it, which are all highly toxic. Similarly, Patanjali shampoo contains urea, artificial color, and fragrance. Biotique has completely hidden all of it. I have tried contacting these [00:04:05] brands, but I did not get any satisfactory response. The bottom line is this, I cannot recommend you any of these shampoos. So, we have seen more than 15 shampoos in three different categories, but none of them have been impressive. So, is there a shampoo in the market which can be used on a daily [00:04:21] basis without worrying about its side effects? Thank god, there are shampoos by Khadi which fall in category number four. These are the shampoos which have no toxic chemicals. These are herbal shampoos in the real sense. They have no toxic chemicals, no strong fragrances, [00:04:38] and not even artificial colors. These are the shampoos which I can recommend to anybody of any hair type without an iota of doubt. Khadi shampoos come in many variants, and all of them are equally good. Now, I want to make this very clear that this video was not [00:04:53] sponsored by Khadi or any other brand for that matter. Whatever I have spoken in this video or any of the previous videos of this series is my honest opinion. I'm not associated with any brand. No brand has paid me to speak all this. So, I hope you have found this [00:05:08] video helpful. I've tried to cover almost all the shampoos available in Indian market, but still if I missed the shampoo which you have been using, I would suggest you to please go through its ingredients, and it would surely fall into one of these four categories. [00:05:24] So, friends, that's all for this video. Please let me know in the comment section which shampoo have you been using, and would you now be changing it or not? And if you want me to continue making these kind of videos, please let me know by giving this video a big thumbs up. If I get good number of likes [00:05:40] on this video, I will continue this series. Probably, I'll make a video on hair oils, face washes, cooking oils, etc. And please do remember to subscribe to my channel. My name is Vivek. I thank you so much for watching.
